newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RESEARCH ALERT - Telefonica de Argentina downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Telefonica de Argentina downgraded.

text.p: Santander Investment announced Tuesday that it had downgraded Telefonica de Argentina to market perform from buy.
Analyst Leslie Marcus wrote in a report the decission was taken on "the fact that the shares are fully valued and the company is near the bottom of our Telco Scorecard."
Santander earnings per ADR estimates remain unchanged at $2.98 and $4.31 for 1997 and 1998, respectively. In 1996 the company reported $2.65.
Telefonica de Argentina is controlled by holding company Cointel which in turn is 50 percent owned by Telefonica de Espana,. Telefonica de Espana is the operator of Telefonica de Argentina.
The remaining 50 percent of Cointel is in the hands of Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holdings SA. CEI is about 40 percent indirectly owned by Citibank.
Telefonica de Argentina is the biggest of the two telephone companies that were formerly part of Entel. The other is Telecom which has about 46 percent of the market.
